the data are consistent with a view that behavioral contrast results from the addition of a less-prefered component in one component of multiple schedules and with a view that reinforcement availability is a critical factor in behavioral contrast in multiple and concurrent reinforcement schedules.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

behavioral contrast can occur when reinforcement availability in one or more components of a multiple schedule is not signalled, but that contrast does not necessarily occur when reinforcement availability is signalled.

reinforcement signalled in one component of multiple or concurrent schedules may be more likely to evoke contrast than would be predicted by a simple account based on reinforcement signalled in the other component being a less-preferred alternative.

The main takeaway from our work is that
reinforcement availability can be signalled without producing behavioral contrast.
reinforcement signalling can have an impact on the allocation of responding between components of concurrent schedules.
behavioral contrast is a powerful process that can be observed under a wide variety of conditions, and that the effects of behavioral contrast are not always predictable.
